species.name: Juvenile Shark
mustRead: asymmetric tail with a long upper lobe
row of five gill slits behind the head
triangular dorsal fin and stiff pectoral wings
species.note: A juvenile has proportionally larger eyes and fins and a slimmer body than an adult.

species.name: Ray
mustRead: flattened disc of wing-like pectoral fins fused to the head
eyes on top with gill slits and mouth underneath
slender trailing tail
species.note: Normally drawn from above; from the side it reads as a thin wafer, so the wing shape must be shown.

species.name: Cave Fish
mustRead: completely eyeless smooth head
pale pink translucent flesh with visible internals
ordinary streamlined fish body and fins

species.name: Goby
mustRead: fused pelvic fins forming a suction disc on the belly
two separate dorsal fins
big blunt head with eyes set high and close together

species.name: Blenny
mustRead: blunt bulldog head with high-set bulging eyes
feathery cirri tufts above the eyes
single long continuous dorsal fin down the whole back

species.name: Dolphin
mustRead: curved sickle-shaped dorsal fin
short beak with an upcurved smiling jawline
crescent tail flukes held horizontally

species.name: Flounder
mustRead: both eyes crowded onto the same side of the head
flat oval body fringed with a continuous fin skirt
twisted asymmetric mouth
species.note: Shown flat-side-on rather than in true lateral profile; a real side view would be a knife edge.

species.name: Mudskipper
mustRead: bulging periscope eyes on top of the head
arm-like pectoral fins propping the body up
two separate dorsal fins raised like sails
species.note: a fish that walks - must be shown out of water on mud, propped on its fins, not swimming

species.name: Grouper
mustRead: huge cavernous mouth with a jutting lower jaw
thick heavy blunt-headed body
rounded paddle tail

species.name: Dugong
mustRead: dolphin-like fluked tail
downturned bristly disc snout
no dorsal fin at all
species.note: often confused with a manatee - dugong has a notched whale fluke, manatee a rounded paddle tail

species.name: Bonefish
mustRead: deeply forked tail
pointed conical snout overhanging the mouth
plain mirror-silver flank

species.name: Barracuda
mustRead: underslung jaw full of exposed dagger teeth
two widely separated dorsal fins
long straight pike-like body

species.name: Reef Fish
mustRead: deep laterally flattened disc body
bright banded colour
forked tail
species.note: generic name - drawn as a representative deep-bodied damselfish/anthias type reef perch

species.name: Shark
mustRead: tall triangular first dorsal fin
asymmetric tail with a longer upper lobe
crescent mouth set under the snout with gill slits behind
species.note: generic name - drawn as a representative requiem shark

species.name: Porpoise
mustRead: blunt rounded head with no beak
small low triangular dorsal fin
stocky short body
species.note: not a dolphin - a porpoise has no beak and a squat triangular fin, not a hooked one

species.name: Cod
mustRead: single barbel hanging from the chin
three separate dorsal fins
pale curved lateral line

species.name: Mackerel
mustRead: wavy dark tiger bars across a steel-blue back
row of small finlets before the forked tail
narrow keeled tail stalk

species.name: Halibut
mustRead: both eyes on the same upper side of the head
continuous fin fringe running right around the body
diamond-elongate flatfish outline
species.note: a flatfish is drawn flank-on (the flat face toward the viewer), not edge-on; both eyes sit on one side

species.name: Reef Shark
mustRead: black or white marked fin tips
slim grey torpedo body
rounded short snout

species.name: Hammerhead Shark
mustRead: flattened T-shaped hammer head with eyes at the outer tips
very tall sickle first dorsal fin
slender grey body

species.name: Manta Ray
mustRead: huge triangular pointed wings wider than the body is long
two horn-like cephalic lobes flanking a wide terminal mouth
thin whip tail with no barb
species.note: a true side view is a flat line - draw from above/front so the wingspan reads; mouth is at the front of the head, not underneath as in stingrays

species.name: Eagle Ray
mustRead: pointed duck-bill snout jutting ahead of the wings
long whip tail far longer than the body
sharply pointed wings, often white-spotted

species.name: Clownfish
mustRead: three white bands edged in black on orange
rounded paddle-shaped fins
blunt stubby snout

species.name: Damselfish
mustRead: deep oval compressed body
single continuous dorsal fin
forked tail
